141268.title: Seocheon Hongwonhang Gizzard Shad and Blue Crab Festival
141268.overview: Late summer is gizzard shad season on Korea's west coast, and Hongwonhang — one of the larger fishing ports in Seocheon — builds a festival around it. Jeoneo is eaten grilled whole or raw as hoe, and is proverbially so fragrant in autumn that a runaway daughter-in-law would come home for it; blue crab, at its meatiest at the same time of year, shares the billing. Entry is free, with a bare-hands fish-catching event at 15,000 won, folk games, and photo spots along the harbour.

229892.title: Yeongcheon Bohyeonsan Starlight Festival
229892.overview: Bohyeonsan holds Korea's largest optical telescope, and this three-day festival at the mountain's astronomical science museum is built around it: astronomy and space-themed exhibitions, hands-on workshops, and performances. The 23rd edition runs 9–11 October. The mountain's altitude and distance from city light make this one of the better places in the country for a dark sky, which is the real reason to make the trip. Free.

639993.title: Yeonsan Jujube Festival
639993.overview: Yeonsan handles more than 40 per cent of the jujubes sold in Korea — the small red date-like fruit used in tea, samgyetang and traditional medicine — and this autumn festival is built around buying them at source. Traders from Yeonsan, Beolgok, Yangchon and neighbouring Unju built the town's reputation by holding back their best fruit for buyers who came in person, and that is still the draw: fresh jujubes below market price, plus stalls, events and performances around Yeonsan Station. Free.

1018971.title: Yanggu Baekbop Festival
1018971.overview: Yanggu sits at the exact geographical centre of the Korean peninsula, and has turned that fact into a festival: baekbop means navel. The 2026 theme is 'Navel Log-in'. It is built around water — hybrid water games and events designed for hot weather — with a street parade, fireworks, nightly concerts and a concert by soldiers from the units stationed in this border county. Free to enter, with some activities charged. Yanggu is close to the DMZ, about three hours from Seoul.

1700219.title: Hampyeong Moaksan Red Spider Lily Festival
1700219.overview: In mid-September the woodland floor around Yongcheonsa Temple turns solid red as hundreds of thousands of spider lilies flower at once — leafless scarlet blooms on bare stems, a plant long associated with Buddhist temple grounds in Korea. The 27th edition leans towards quiet rather than spectacle: forest-therapy and meditation programmes along the Moaksan trails, walking routes through the flowering colonies, and local food. Free to enter. The bloom is short and weather-dependent, so check timing before travelling.

1718491.title: Seorak Cultural Festival
1718491.overview: Sokcho's oldest festival, running since 1966 and now in its 61st year, held beneath Seoraksan at the start of the autumn foliage season. The 2026 theme is 'Seorak, Turning Colour Together'. At its heart is Seorak Sosa, a mountain rite performed at the very first festival and still held today — now with narration and storytelling added so that visitors can follow what is happening. The programme also includes a climb up Dalmabong, a trail otherwise closed to the public, a mountain concert, and a street parade led by residents, schools and local arts groups rather than professional performers. Free.
1718491.place: Sokcho Expo Lawn Plaza and the Seorak Rodeo Street area
1718491.sponsor: Sokcho City · Sokcho Culture and Tourism Foundation

2547013.title: Nosang-noriya: Traditional Street Performance Parade, Jeonju Hanok Village
2547013.overview: A free street performance that turns the main road of Jeonju Hanok Village into an open-air stage every Saturday afternoon. The centrepiece is gijeop-nori, a Jeonju tradition in which enormous dragon banners are hoisted and swung overhead by teams of performers — a display of strength and balance as much as ceremony — set to the drums and gongs of a pungmul percussion troupe. Short satirical madang plays and displays of traditional acrobatics fill out the hour, and visitors are taught to sing along to 'Mandure Sori', a Jeonju work song passed down orally among rice farmers. No ticket, no seating: it moves along Taejo-ro between Namcheongyo Bridge and Gyeonggijeon Shrine, so you can simply join the crowd.
2547013.place: Taejo-ro, Jeonju Hanok Village (Namcheongyo Bridge to Gyeonggijeon Shrine)
2547013.sponsor: Jeonju City · Jeonbuk Culture and Tourism Foundation

2614760.title: Gyeongju Heritage Night Walk
2614760.overview: Gyeongju was the capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years, and this event opens its monuments after dark. The 2026 edition is subtitled 'Fragments — What We Have Kept, and What We Will Keep', and spreads across Woljeonggyo Bridge, Gyerim Forest, Gyochon Hanok Village and Gyeongju Eupseong Fortress. Expect illuminated architecture, performances and hands-on programmes at each site. Most of it is free; a few individual programmes charge. For a visitor this is the easiest way to see Gyeongju's heritage sites lit at night, when they are markedly less crowded than by day.
2614760.place: Woljeonggyo Bridge, Gyochon Hanok Village, Cheomseongdae and Gyeongju Eupseong Fortress
2614760.sponsor: Korea Heritage Service · Gyeongsangbuk-do · Gyeongju City

2661307.title: Korea International Ocean Film Festival (KIOFF)
2661307.overview: A film festival devoted entirely to the sea, held at the Busan Cinema Center. It began in 2015 as 'Sea & See' and has run under its current name since 2018. The programme ranges from the scale and strangeness of the ocean to the crises now facing it, with the stated aim of imagining a future in which people and the sea coexist. Screenings are 5,000 won a ticket — cheap by festival standards — and the venue is the same landmark building that hosts the Busan International Film Festival.
2661307.sponsor: Busan Metropolitan City · Korea Ocean Business Corporation

2755115.title: Goyang Food and Beer Festival
2755115.overview: Goyang's food-and-drink festival, now in its seventh year, held along the pedestrian street of La Festa in Ilsan. Craft beer and food stalls run alongside live music and hands-on activities, with a dedicated food-truck zone and beer zone. It is a city-centre street festival rather than a destination event — easy to reach from Seoul on Subway Line 3, and free to enter, with food and drink paid for individually.
2755115.fee: Free entry (food and drink charged separately)

2758030.title: Dangjin Haenaru Sweet Potato Festival
2758030.overview: Dangjin's sweet potatoes grow in yellow-ochre soil under sea wind from the west coast, which the region credits for their sweetness and dry, floury texture. The ninth edition of this harvest festival sells them direct from the growers below market price, alongside food stalls doing sweet potato fritters, dig-your-own plots for children, craft workshops, a regional produce market and stage performances. Free to enter, with some programmes charged.

2849159.title: Yeonsu Neungheodae Culture Festival
2849159.overview: Neungheodae is the point on the Incheon coast where Baekje envoys set out by sea for China some 1,600 years ago, and the festival built around it centres on a costumed Baekje Envoy Parade. The 14th edition adds an awards ceremony, headline concerts, fireworks, and participation booths run by residents. The main draw for 2026 is a drone light show of about 2,000 drones on the theme 'Neungheodae, Voyage of Light' — the largest the district has staged — reinterpreting those ancient sea crossings. Free.

2859297.title: Festival Gwangmyeong
2859297.overview: Gwangmyeong closes an eight-lane road beside Cheolsan Station and turns it into a street festival for two days. The GM Live main stage runs eleven acts: singer-songwriter 10cm headlines the first night with Daybreak, Jack Kingkong, Asrai and Asadal, and Korean rock veteran Kim Jong-seo the second, with Romantic Punch, Bulnabang Star Sausage Club and others. On the closed road itself there is a random-play dance, street karaoke, a bubble show and stilt performers, plus a civic parade, youth busking and market stalls run by local social enterprises. Free.
2859297.place: The eight-lane road at Cheolsan Station

3340159.title: Cheongchun-daero Youth Street Festival
3340159.overview: A day-long street festival on the open-air stage at Seoul Children's Grand Park, run by Gwangjin-gu and programmed largely by students from nearby Konkuk and Sejong universities. Club performances, busking, a talk show and headline acts run through the afternoon, with a flea market and craft stalls from young local makers. Free, and easy to combine with the park itself, which is one of the largest green spaces in eastern Seoul.
3340159.place: Open Stage, Seoul Children's Grand Park

3351268.title: Dongdaemun-gu Beer Festival
3351268.overview: A late-summer beer festival on the waterside at Jangan 1 Waterfront Park in eastern Seoul, held in the last week of August. Craft breweries and food trucks set up along the water, with jazz performances, outdoor film screenings and photo zones. Entry is free; drinks and food are paid for individually. It is a neighbourhood event rather than a tourist attraction, which is rather the point of going.
3351268.fee: Free entry (drinks and food charged separately)

3354966.title: Yongsan Heritage Night Walk
3354966.overview: For a few evenings each year Hyochang Park — an ordinary neighbourhood park in central Seoul most of the time — is lit and staged as a memorial to the Korean independence movement. Eight independence activists are buried here, including Kim Gu, and the programme builds around them: illuminated grounds, performances, exhibitions, guided commentary and hands-on activities. It runs into the night deliberately, so that the park reads differently than it does by day. Local schools, universities, veterans' associations and arts organisations each contribute their own programme rather than a single organiser producing everything.

3368584.title: Busan Youth Week
3368584.overview: A three-day festival on Busan's Pier 1 marking Korea's Youth Day, programmed by young directors from the city under the theme 'The Faces of Busan'. The staging is immersive rather than a conventional stage-and-audience format, and the setting — a working port pier in the old town, close to Jagalchi and BIFF Square — is part of the appeal. Free, and open to anyone, not only Busan residents. Programmes are in Korean.

3497353.title: Busan Sea Library 2026
3497353.overview: An open-air reading festival on the sand at Dadaepo Beach, at the mouth of the Nakdong River — the beach best known for its sunsets and its musical fountain. Public libraries, bookshops and publishers set up outdoors with reading programmes and cultural events, running from mid-afternoon into the evening. Free. It is weather-dependent and the schedule can shift, so confirm before making the trip out to Dadaepo, which is at the far western end of Metro Line 1.

3581975.title: Open Port Christmas: Bulmeong
3581975.overview: A year-end campfire festival on the old open-port waterfront in Incheon, where visitors and their dogs sit around fires to see out the year. Bulmeong — roughly 'fire-gazing' — is the Korean word for staring into a campfire doing nothing, and the event takes it literally: a campfire zone with winter snacks for those who book ahead, lights and decorations, and a stamp trail whose completion triggers a donation to abandoned-dog shelters. There is an indoor play area and a 1,650 m² off-leash zone for dogs. Free.

4107768.title: Korea National Contemporary Dance Company: Site and Fold — Yeongwol
4107768.overview: A mixed-reality dance performance by choreographer Song Ju-won, staged in a former mining-country gallery in Yeongwol. The work is built around mourning what has disappeared or is disappearing — human and non-human alike — and the audience moves through it wearing augmented- and virtual-reality equipment, becoming participants rather than spectators. Because the piece is largely movement and image rather than text, the language barrier is low. Admission is free, an open rehearsal runs at 19:00, and the last performance each day is followed by a talk with the artists.

4108250.title: Wonju Book Festival 2026: Books Met in the Street
4108250.overview: A weekend reading festival that deliberately spills out of the library and into the city — small neighbourhood libraries, independent bookshops and open-air reading rooms across Wonju. The programme includes talks by Korean authors Ye So-yeon, Baek Yu-yeon and Kim Geun-hee, a staged reading for children, and outdoor performances and workshops. Almost everything is in Korean, so the draw for a foreign visitor is the outdoor reading rooms and the atmosphere rather than the talks.

4108258.title: Sejong and Paik: Hangeul Culture Special Exhibition 2026
4108258.overview: An exhibition pairing two Korean innovators five centuries apart: King Sejong, who created the Hangeul alphabet in the 1440s, and Nam June Paik, who invented video art in the 1960s. The argument is that both remade how people communicate. It runs from 9 October — Hangeul Day — to 8 November at the Biennale Hall in Sejong City, the administrative capital named after the king. Free, with volunteer-led tours at 14:00 and 16:00, Tuesday to Sunday. Tours are in Korean.

4108260.title: HUG RUN 2026
4108260.overview: A charity run against child abuse, held at Peace Plaza in Seoul's World Cup Park. Participants choose a 3 km, 6 km or 11.19 km course. It is run as a virtual event with a registration cap of 3,000, and the entry fee goes in full to supporting children who have suffered abuse. Registrants receive a running kit with a T-shirt and finisher's medal, and there are prize draws for entry numbers and for posting a finish on social media.
4108260.place: Peace Plaza, Sangam World Cup Park

4108615.title: Donggang Doomchit
4108615.overview: A one-day outdoor lifestyle festival on the banks of the Donggang River in Yeongwol, run by and for the county's young residents. There is an outdoor reading garden, a market of young Yeongwol brands, a food club built around local produce, and a live radio programme broadcasting listeners' stories and interviews from the riverbank. Birdwatching, mindfulness sessions, hula dancing and caricature drawing run through the day, with evening sets from Korean indie acts including Yozoh, Soran and Seoul Bossa Society. Free.

4108758.title: Seven Bridges Tour 2026
4108758.overview: A 77 km cycling event across Busan's sea bridges — the only day of the year these spans open to bicycles. The route starts on Gwangan Bridge and links Busan Harbour Bridge, Namhang Bridge and Eulsukdo Bridge, riding above the water on roads normally closed to anything but cars. For non-cyclists there is a separate Gwangan Bridge walking programme, plus wellness activities and a food lounge around Yongho Byeolbit Park. Paid entry, and Busan residents get 50 per cent off.
4108758.place: Across Busan — major sea bridges and the city centre
4108758.fee: Seven Bridges Tour 100,000 won (early bird 80,000 won) · Good Morning Bridge Walking 10,000 won · 50% off for Busan residents

4109218.title: Gunwi Samgungnyusa Family Walk with Ingaksa Temple
4109218.overview: A family walking event at Ingaksa, the temple where the monk Iryeon is believed to have written the Samgungnyusa — the 13th-century chronicle that preserves Korea's foundation myths and much of what is known about the Three Kingdoms period. The fifth edition offers 5 km and 10 km routes through the countryside around the temple in late October, with concerts by Korean trot singers Hong Won-bin, Park Seo-jin and Kim Tae-yeon at the finish. Paid entry from primary-school age; under-18s must be accompanied.
4109218.fee: 5 km 7,000 won · 10 km 10,000 won (primary-school age and above)
4109218.sponsor: Gunwi County · Gunwi County Sports Council · Yeongnam Ilbo

4109305.title: Moonlight Workout Busan Challenge
4109305.overview: An outdoor fitness event held on autumn evenings across three Busan parks — Busan Citizens Park, the North Port waterfront and Hwamyeong Ecological Park. Sessions are led by well-known fitness instructors and cover gymnastics, yoga, circuit training, zumba and children's classes, interspersed with taekwondo and cheerleading displays, busking and comedy. There are also fitness-test booths, archery, basketball, bowling and golf try-outs, and a random-play dance challenge. Free, informal, and one of the more unusual things to do in Busan after dark.
4109305.place: Busan Citizens Park · North Port Waterfront Park · Hwamyeong Ecological Park

4109423.title: U-Plef Youth Festival, Namyangju
4109423.overview: A one-day youth festival on the Han River at Sampae, Namyangju. Hands-on booths run by young organisers open at 13:00, a local talent stage follows in the late afternoon, and the evening closes with performances by rapper Gaogaii and singer Kim Na-young. Food trucks, a flea market and a non-alcoholic beer bar run alongside. Free, on the riverside about 40 minutes east of central Seoul.
4109423.place: Sampae District Water Park, Han River Park
